ANN-M1.text: ANN-M1 / model Question: Mr Aliyu puts 4 counters down. He touches each once: 1, 2, 3, 4. Then he adds 2: 5, 6. So 4 + 2 = 6. Grace checks by moving each counter once. Find the question: Textbook annual 241. Answer: Mr Aliyu puts 4 counters down. He touches each once: 1, 2, 3, 4. Then he adds 2: 5, 6. So 4 + 2 = 6. Grace checks by moving each counter once.

ANN-G1.text: ANN-G1 / guided Question: Put 3 counters down. Add 2. Count them together. Explain how you avoid counting one twice. Find the question: Textbook annual 241. Answer: 5 counters; touch or move each once.

ANN-I1.text: ANN-I1 / independent Question: Draw 5 circles in your workbook. Add 3 more. How many altogether? Explain your check. Find the question: Textbook annual 246; Workbook annual 167. Answer: 8; 5 + 3 = 8. Count each circle once.

ANN-M2.text: ANN-M2 / model Question: Mr Aliyu puts 7 counters down. He moves 3 away. 4 remain: 7 - 3 = 4. He checks 3 + 4 = 7. Adamu makes sure each friend can see. Find the question: Textbook annual 242. Answer: Mr Aliyu puts 7 counters down. He moves 3 away. 4 remain: 7 - 3 = 4. He checks 3 + 4 = 7. Adamu makes sure each friend can see.

ANN-G2.text: ANN-G2 / guided Question: Put 8 counters down. Move 2 away. Say the remaining number. Check by putting the parts together. Find the question: Textbook annual 242. Answer: 6 remain; 2 + 6 = 8. ANNUAL TEXTBOOK 274 | ANNUAL LEARNING AND SUPPORT

ANN-I2.text: ANN-I2 / independent Question: Draw 9 circles. Cross out 4. How many remain? Write a matching subtraction sentence. Find the question: Textbook annual 247; Workbook annual 168. Answer: 5; 9 - 4 = 5.

ANN-M3.text: ANN-M3 / model Question: Mr Aliyu aligns the ends of two safe strips. One extends farther: it is longer. Aishatu waits while John feels the aligned ends. Then they fold one paper circle into two equal matching parts: each is a half. Find the question: Textbook annual 243. Answer: Mr Aliyu aligns the ends of two safe strips. One extends farther: it is longer. Aishatu waits while John feels the aligned ends. Then they fold one paper circle into two equal matching parts: each is a half.

ANN-G3.text: ANN-G3 / guided Question: Use two safe strips. Align one end. Say which is longer, shorter or equal. Fold a paper circle into two equal matching parts. Explain why the parts are halves. Find the question: Textbook annual 243. Answer: Comparison depends on strips; compare from one baseline. Two equal matching parts make halves.

ANN-I3.text: ANN-I3 / independent Question: Draw a circle. Show two equal halves. With safe strips, compare two lengths from the same starting line. Tell an adult what you found. Find the question: Textbook annual 248; Workbook annual 169. Answer: Two equal parts of the circle; accept any straight diameter forming two equal halves. Length comparison depends on actual strips.

ANN-R.text: ANN-R / recall Question: Explain a count check and subtraction check. Find the question: Textbook annual 244. Answer: Count each once; recombine removed and remaining parts. ANNUAL TEXTBOOK 275 | ANNUAL LEARNING AND SUPPORT

ANN-H.text: ANN-H / help/recheck Question: Use 2 counters, add 1; then try 2 and 2. Find the question: Textbook annual 244. Answer: 3 in model; 4 in new unaided recheck after support.

ANN-F.text: ANN-F / fresh Question: Start with 6, add 3. Check another way. Find the question: Textbook annual 244. Answer: 9; count all or count on; 6 + 3 = 9.

ANN-C1.text: ANN-C1 / independent Question: Say the number just after 8. Draw 6 circles. Put 5 large counters into a row and check each once. Sort 4 safe objects by one feature and tell your rule. Find the question: Textbook annual 249; Workbook annual 170. Answer: 9; six circles; count 5 once each; consistent stated sorting rule.

ANN-C2.text: ANN-C2 / independent Question: Write 24 as tens and ones. Work out 5 + 4. Draw 8 circles and remove 3. Fold one paper circle into two equal matching halves. Explain one answer. Find the question: Textbook annual 250; Workbook annual 171. Answer: 2 tens and 4 ones; 9; 5; two equal matching parts. Accept a valid check.

ANN-C3.text: ANN-C3 / independent Question: Use pretend value cards 5 and 2. Find their total. Align two safe strips and compare length. Name a rectangle you draw. Say what comes after morning in our day: afternoon or night. Find the question: Textbook annual 251; Workbook annual 172. Answer: 7 pretend units; length depends on strips; closed four-straight-sided rectangle with opposite sides equal and square corners; afternoon. ANNUAL TEXTBOOK 276 | ANNUAL LEARNING AND SUPPORT

ANN-C4.text: ANN-C4 / independent Question: Write 31 in tens and ones. Work out 8 + 2 and 9 - 4. Draw four equal quarters in a square. Use two safe real objects to test which is heavier; explain what you observed. Ask two invented roles their age in completed years and record their replies with different labels. Find the question: Textbook annual 252; Workbook annual 173. Answer: 3 tens and 1 one; 10; 5; four equal-area parts of a square, including four equal strips; actual balance/weight observation determines heavier/lighter/equal; accurately labelled fictional replies after asking.

AI-M1.text: AI-M1 / model Question: What is AI? Can its answer be wrong? Find the question: Textbook annual 269. Answer: A computer tool made by people; uses patterns learned from many examples to make replies; not a person; has no feelings; replies can be wrong.

AI-G.text: AI-G / guided Question: Count the four printed counters and correct the pretend five. Find the question: Textbook annual 270. Answer: 4; five is wrong; touch each of the four once.

AI-M2.text: AI-M2 / model Question: Three counters and two more. Find the question: Textbook annual 271. Answer: 5; 3 + 2 = 5.

AI-I.text: AI-I / independent Question: Ask about two counters and one more; verify three. Find the question: Textbook annual 271. Answer: A clear non-private question stating 2 and 1 more; verify 3 with objects.

AI-F.text: AI-F / fresh Question: Count six printed counters and independently correct pretend four. Find the question: Textbook annual 272. Answer: 6; four is wrong. Touch each once and explain. ANNUAL TEXTBOOK 277 | ANNUAL LEARNING AND SUPPORT

AI-H.text: AI-H / help/recheck Question: Check two counters together, then a new set of three. Find the question: Textbook annual 272. Answer: 2 in model; 3 in unaided recheck after support.

AI-R.text: AI-R / recall Question: Recall the checking and privacy rules. Find the question: Textbook annual 272. Answer: Ask clearly; use invented non-private maths; check answers with own maths and adult support.

AI-W1.text: AI-W1 / independent Question: Ask an adult a clear question about 2 counters and 1 more. The adult reads: Pretend AI says three. Check with counters. Draw or write your check. Use no private information. Find the question: Textbook annual 271; Workbook annual 174. Answer: 3; clear question and one-to-one checking.

AI-W2.text: AI-W2 / independent Question: These dots are the whole set. Pretend AI says four. Count each dot once. Write the correct number and explain to an adult. Find the question: Textbook annual 272; Workbook annual 175. Answer: 6; four is wrong; count each of six once.

LEG-P1-R1-1.text: LEG-P1-R1-1 / independent Question: Write the number for no objects. Find the question: Textbook annual 253; Workbook annual 176. Answer: 0

LEG-P1-R1-2.text: LEG-P1-R1-2 / independent Question: Order 8, 3 and 6 from smallest to largest. Find the question: Textbook annual 253; Workbook annual 176. Answer: 3, 6, 8 ANNUAL TEXTBOOK 278 | ANNUAL LEARNING AND SUPPORT

LEG-P1-R1-3.text: LEG-P1-R1-3 / independent Question: What comes after 59? Find the question: Textbook annual 255; Workbook annual 178. Answer: 60

LEG-P1-R1-4.text: LEG-P1-R1-4 / independent Question: 2 tens and 7 ones make __. Find the question: Textbook annual 255; Workbook annual 178. Answer: 27

LEG-P1-R1-5.text: LEG-P1-R1-5 / independent Question: Draw four equal parts of a square and shade one. Find the question: Textbook annual 256; Workbook annual 179. Answer: One quarter shaded; four equal-area parts.

LEG-P1-R1-6.text: LEG-P1-R1-6 / independent Question: Show 9 objects and explain how you checked. Find the question: Textbook annual 254; Workbook annual 177. Answer: Exactly nine; touch or move each once.

LEG-P1-R2-1.text: LEG-P1-R2-1 / independent Question: 3 + 4 + 1 = __. Find the question: Textbook annual 256; Workbook annual 179. Answer: 8

LEG-P1-R2-2.text: LEG-P1-R2-2 / independent Question: 17 - 8 = __. Find the question: Textbook annual 257; Workbook annual 180. Answer: 9

LEG-P1-R2-3.text: LEG-P1-R2-3 / independent Question: 24 + 12 = __. Find the question: Textbook annual 257; Workbook annual 180. Answer: 36 ANNUAL TEXTBOOK 279 | ANNUAL LEARNING AND SUPPORT

LEG-P1-R2-4.text: LEG-P1-R2-4 / independent Question: 6 + __ = 10. Find the question: Textbook annual 258; Workbook annual 181. Answer: 4

LEG-P1-R2-5.text: LEG-P1-R2-5 / independent Question: In this invented token game, k is a pretend unit, not a price. Pretend cost 8k; pay 10k. Find and check change. Find the question: Textbook annual 259; Workbook annual 182. Answer: 2k; 8k + 2k = 10k.

LEG-P1-R2-6.text: LEG-P1-R2-6 / independent Question: Draw or show why 7 + 6 = 13. Find the question: Textbook annual 258; Workbook annual 181. Answer: Two sets total thirteen; or count on six from seven.

LEG-P1-R3-1.text: LEG-P1-R3-1 / independent Question: Three paths measure 5, 2 and 7 repeats of the same paper strip. Order their lengths from shortest. Find the question: Textbook annual 259; Workbook annual 182. Answer: 2, 5, 7

LEG-P1-R3-2.text: LEG-P1-R3-2 / independent Question: What comes after afternoon: morning or evening? Find the question: Textbook annual 260; Workbook annual 183. Answer: evening

LEG-P1-R3-3.text: LEG-P1-R3-3 / independent Question: Handle a safe ball-shaped model. Name its solid shape. Find the question: Textbook annual 260; Workbook annual 183. Answer: sphere ANNUAL TEXTBOOK 280 | ANNUAL LEARNING AND SUPPORT

LEG-P1-R3-4.text: LEG-P1-R3-4 / independent Question: How many corners has a square? Find the question: Textbook annual 261; Workbook annual 184. Answer: 4

LEG-P1-R3-5.text: LEG-P1-R3-5 / independent Question: Compare two safe objects by weight. Show your method. Find the question: Textbook annual 261; Workbook annual 184. Answer: Use a balance or safe lifting to test the two actual safe objects. Accept heavier, lighter or equal weight when it matches the observation; do not infer weight from a picture.

LEG-P1-R3-6.text: LEG-P1-R3-6 / independent Question: Invented ages are 6, 7, 7, 6. How many pupils are 7? Explain. Find the question: Textbook annual 262; Workbook annual 185. Answer: 2; count the two records equal to seven.

LEG-P1-A1-1.text: LEG-P1-A1-1 / independent Question: Write eighty-two in digits. Find the question: Textbook annual 263; Workbook annual 186. Answer: 82

LEG-P1-A1-2.text: LEG-P1-A1-2 / independent Question: Complete: 8, 9, __, __. Find the question: Textbook annual 263; Workbook annual 186. Answer: 10, 11

LEG-P1-A1-3.text: LEG-P1-A1-3 / independent Question: 15 = __ ten and __ ones. Find the question: Textbook annual 264; Workbook annual 187. Answer: 1 ten, 5 ones ANNUAL TEXTBOOK 281 | ANNUAL LEARNING AND SUPPORT

LEG-P1-A1-4.text: LEG-P1-A1-4 / independent Question: 8 + 7 = __. Find the question: Textbook annual 264; Workbook annual 187. Answer: 15

LEG-P1-A1-5.text: LEG-P1-A1-5 / independent Question: 16 - 9 = __. Show a check. Find the question: Textbook annual 265; Workbook annual 188. Answer: 7; 7 + 9 = 16.

LEG-P1-A1-6.text: LEG-P1-A1-6 / independent Question: __ + 4 = 9. Explain the blank. Find the question: Textbook annual 265; Workbook annual 188. Answer: 5; 9 − 4 = 5 or count on.

LEG-P1-A2-1.text: LEG-P1-A2-1 / independent Question: Draw a rectangle and show one half. Find the question: Textbook annual 266; Workbook annual 189. Answer: Two equal-area parts, one selected.

LEG-P1-A2-2.text: LEG-P1-A2-2 / independent Question: In this invented token game, k is a pretend unit, not a price. Pretend tokens 10k + 5k total __. Find the question: Textbook annual 266; Workbook annual 189. Answer: 15k

LEG-P1-A2-3.text: LEG-P1-A2-3 / independent Question: Handle a safe rectangular box model. Name its solid shape. Find the question: Textbook annual 267; Workbook annual 190. Answer: cuboid ANNUAL TEXTBOOK 282 | ANNUAL LEARNING AND SUPPORT

LEG-P1-A2-4.text: LEG-P1-A2-4 / independent Question: Write morning, night, afternoon in day order. Find the question: Textbook annual 267; Workbook annual 190. Answer: morning, afternoon, night

LEG-P1-A2-5.text: LEG-P1-A2-5 / independent Question: Measure a book with a repeated paper strip. Record and explain. Find the question: Textbook annual 268; Workbook annual 191. Answer: Pupil’s repeated equal-unit count, with no gaps or overlaps.

LEG-P1-A2-6.text: LEG-P1-A2-6 / independent Question: Ask two invented pupil roles their ages in completed years. Record each reply with a different label. Compare the ages. Find the question: Textbook annual 268; Workbook annual 191. Answer: Two labelled age records and a correct comparison.

ANN-D.text: ANN-D / delayed Question: Delayed: 4 + 3 and 6 - 2. Find the question: Textbook annual 284. Answer: 7 and 4; show and explain methods.

AI-D.text: AI-D / delayed Question: Delayed: five real counters, invented reply six. Recall privacy rule. Find the question: Textbook annual 284. Answer: 5; six is wrong; check each once. Use non-private invented examples and trusted adult help. ANNUAL TEXTBOOK 283 | ANNUAL LEARNING AND SUPPORT

limits: Source task linkage is partial assessment evidence, not certification of all aspects or actual pupil mastery. Physical coin recognition/tracing, natural-unit measurement and collection remain conditional as printed and in attributed prior reviews.
